comment: Appeal for change Good evening/morning, Thank you for taking the time to read my email. I will be as brief as possible. I also hope to join tomorrow evening's meeting to speak to this issue. My name is Yvette Melby Garcia and I would like to tell you about my recent walk in Sugarhouse park and appeal to you, as the city council, for change. Two Saturdays ago, November 21, 2020, my friend and I took a walk in Sugarhouse Park to enjoy the afternoon sunshine. I had my 9 month old baby and dog, and she had her dog as well. As we walked the popular circle with many other Salt Lake folk that day, we were accosted by a long chain of vehicles carrying signs and flags in support of Q and Donald Trump. My friend and I were wearing masks and many people in that group shouted at us to take off our masks. This was only slightly alarming compared to what we came across next. Shortly after rounding the last turn, we saw that most of the vehicles had pulled over. Among those exiting those vehicles were several men carrying what appeared to be high caliber assault rifles. They stood by, along the side of the road, in a threatening manner. One boy, who appeared to be underage, followed us as we walked, after I told him several times to back away and stop following us. As we had to drive back through this rally to exit the park, the friend who I was with, who is Black, was verbally accosted by another armed man who said to her, "we are going to kill Black people." He also used vulgar language. There are so many layers to this event that are troubling, it would take some time to break them all down. The most notable, in addition to the racially charged threats, is that my friend and I, two women and a baby, were unable to go safely on a walk in our own public neighborhood park. For this reason I am appealing to you today, as our city council, to encourage those in a position to do so, to put in place an ordinance or a law that prohibits the use of the open carry of weapons in public parks. I strongly bell've that we can all agree, regardless of political view or party, race or gender, that we should all feel safe enough in our neighborhoods and public spaces to take a sunny Saturday afternoon walk in the park. In support of this measure, I have created a petition and am currently collecting signatures from concerned community members. I am happy to share these with you once collected. Thank you so much for your time and attention to this matter. Longtime Salt Lake City Community Member, Yvette Melby Garcia
